published_partition_evidence: GA102 die layout: 6 GPC × (12 SM/GPC) on the full die; L2 is 6 MB total split across 6 partitions (1 MB per partition) on the RTX 3090 Ti consumer SKU. NVIDIA Ampere GA102 whitepaper (2020) Figure 3 + the device_properties.json::entries[0].note field's citation of `workloads/simbench_bw/run_suite.py::_static_card_num_l2_slices_for_props` (the existing static-card identity, pinned at 6 partitions for sm_86 RTX 3090 Ti). The audit does NOT add NEW external citations; it ratifies the existing in-repo evidence chain.
slice_hash_model_documentation: The walker at tools/hrd_profiler/observation_builder.py line 391 routes sector_id to slice (sector_id % num_l2_slices). This is a COARSE APPROXIMATION of the real GA102 L2 partition hash. The real hardware uses a proprietary address-bit XOR-based hash (with possible page-coloring + ECC-stripe interleave effects) that is not publicly documented. The modulo identity is a defensible lower-bound approximation: it gives each slice an equal share of sector IDs and treats slice routing as deterministic per-sector. Possible biases vs the real hash: (a) real hash may cluster certain sector-ID-modulo-X patterns into one slice for certain access strides (partition camping), causing real per-slice load to be MORE uneven than the modulo model; (b) real hash may use upper-bit XOR to spread regular strides better, causing real per-slice load to be MORE even than the modulo model. The net direction depends on the access pattern.
modeling_uncertainty_documentation: Classification rationale: `published_partition_count=6` is well-supported (vendor-documented + cross-referenced in the existing in-repo manifest + run_suite static-card identity), so the partition COUNT is `published_exact_match` quality. However, the `chosen_slice_hash_model=sector_id_mod_num_l2_slices` is a documented APPROXIMATION because the real GA102 hash is proprietary. The audit overall classifies as `published_approximation` (the weaker of the two; the hash-model approximation is the binding uncertainty). The audit does NOT claim `published_exact_match` because that would require explicit hardware-documentation evidence of the hash function, which is not publicly available. The audit does NOT classify as `unverified` because the partition count itself is well-documented and the modulo hash is a defensible-bias-bounded approximation.
